- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; increase forecast to catch upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward 1–3 days later.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >5% for 3+ consecutive days), apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is trending upward from prior 10–15 days, model often misses early momentum; shift forecast up 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag in direction; align forecast with sentiment swing midpoint, not peak.
